items.name: Power plugs & voltage
items.description: Malta uses the UK-style Type G plug (three rectangular pins) at 230 V / 50 Hz. US devices need a Type G adapter; US hairdryers/straighteners also need a voltage converter unless rated 100–240 V. Laptops/phone chargers are almost always dual-voltage — adapter only.
items.notes: Type G / 230V / 50Hz is standard across VisitMalta and UK-plug references. Hotel rooms have limited sockets near the desk — a 2-USB adapter block is worth packing.

items.name: Mobile data — SIM & eSIM
items.address: MLA arrivals: Epic shop in the terminal; GO and Melita in town shops
items.description: Three operators: GO, Melita, Epic — all with good 4G/5G. US phones roam at painful rates, so buy local: Epic has an airport counter (SIM ~€10, e.g. 5 GB/28-day packs); Melita Pass L 25 GB ≈ €12; GO Smart Unlimited ≈ €15.99/28 days. Alternatively install a travel eSIM (Airalo/Holafly/Nomad) before departure and land connected.
items.notes: 2026 operator bundles via guide aggregations (roafly checked 27 Sep 2026: Epic Value Pack €10.99/10 GB/28d, Melita Pockit L €12/25 GB, GO Smart Unlimited €15.99). Prices drift — confirm at the counter. Hotel Wi-Fi covers most of the day; a small eSIM is enough for maps+buses.

items.name: Money — euro, cards, tipping
items.description: Currency is the euro (€). Cards/contactless (Visa/Mastercard, Apple/Google Pay) are accepted almost everywhere including buses and taxis; keep €20–40 cash for pastizzerie, kiosks and tips. Tipping: round up or ~10% in restaurants if service isn't included; €1–2 for taxi drivers; no US-style obligation.
items.notes: USD is not accepted. Tell your bank the travel dates; Revolut/Wise cards are widely used by travelers. Tipping norms from community consensus + VisitMalta guidance.

items.name: VAT & prices
items.description: Standard VAT is 18% and is always included in displayed prices (no US-style tax added at the till). Reduced rates: 7% accommodation, 5% museum/concert admission and some foods, 0% most groceries and medicines.
items.notes: PwC professional summary (cfr.gov.mt rates page errored on last attempt). Prices-you-see-are-prices-you-pay is standard practice.

items.name: Emergencies & health
items.address: Mater Dei Hospital (Msida) is the main hospital; polyclinics in Qawra/Buġibba area
items.description: EU emergency number 112 (police/ambulance/fire). US health insurance does not cover you abroad — buy travel medical insurance. Pharmacies are plentiful and pharmacists can prescribe for minor ailments; bring a personal supply of any prescription meds in original packaging. Tap water is desalinated and safe but tastes flat — bottled water is the norm.
items.notes: 112 is EU-standard; US Embassy Malta (Ta' Qali National Park Street, Attard ATD 4000 — same complex as the tournament venue; +356 2561 4000) per mt.usembassy.gov.

items.name: Language
items.description: Maltese and English are both official; virtually everyone in tourism speaks fluent English (it's the medium of schooling and media). Maltese is Semitic with heavy Italian loanwords — 'Grazzi' (thanks), 'Bonġu' (hello), 'Saħħa' (cheers/bye). Road signs are bilingual; place names appear in Maltese (Il-Qawra, Ħ'Attard).
items.notes: No language barrier for a US traveler; learning three Maltese words is a crowd-pleaser.

items.name: Weather, 13–19 Oct
items.description: October averages: daytime highs ≈ 25 °C (77 °F), lows ≈ 21 °C (70 °F), sea ≈ 22–24 °C (still swimmable), ≈ 7 hours of sunshine. Rain comes in short bursts, usually evenings; one light layer for night events is enough. UV is still moderate — sunscreen for beach days.
items.notes: Averages from holiday-weather.com (Malta October: 25/22, sea 24) cross-checked against maltauncovered (17–24 °C day) and ManicMalta ('highs around 25 °C, sea still warm enough to swim'). Day-of forecasts: check Malta Airport weather/Met Office before packing.

items.name: Accommodation eco-tax
items.price_range: €1.50 per person per night (18+), cap €22.50 per visit
items.description: A small environmental contribution collected by hotels — €1.50/night per adult since 1 July 2026 (up to €22.50 per stay). For 6 nights: €9. Often invoiced separately at check-out even when the room is pre-paid.
items.notes: Verified against the Malta Tourism Authority guidelines PDF in the 24 Sep 2026 session (effective 1 Jul 2026). Budget it in the expense planner.

items.name: US customs & re-entry (short trip)
items.description: Returning to the US: standard personal exemption applies ($800 goods if eligible); declare purchases. Global Entry/Mobile Passport cuts the arrival queue at SFO. Malta is not a US-VWP country for Maltese entry to the US, but as a US citizen you need no visa for Malta (≤90 days) — passport should be valid 3+ months beyond departure; EES entry/exit fingerprinting applies on first EU entry (system live since 10 Apr 2026 — see logistics.html).
items.notes: CBP exemption figure is standard; EES date per prior session's EU-source check — re-confirm 'fully operational' status at ec.europa.eu T-7.

items.name: Driving & transport habits
items.description: Malta drives on the LEFT (British heritage). Roundabouts are aggressive; speed limits 50–80 km/h. For this trip you won't drive — buses, ferries and Bolt cover everything. jaywalking is common but crossings exist on the promenade roads; traffic moves fast on Triq il-Qawra.
items.notes: Look RIGHT first when crossing — the classic US-tourist trap.
